en: (Mantra-core) May the illustrious Rāmacandra, who is accompanied by [Sītā], who is unwearied, and who is denoted by the syllable Oṃ, protect me with auspiciousness.
The sovereign of kings, the sustainer of the entire world, who has assumed his vows through humble prostration, is the remover of mental anguish.
Obeisance today to the Infinite One, whose majesty is great, who is the abode of the ultimate truth, and whose body is the end of delusion.
To him who has assumed a beautiful form for the welfare of the world, who grants the desires of his devotees, and who restrains those who act against them.
To the Lord of Sacrifice, the protector of all dharma, the bestower of liberation, and the slayer of the wicked asuras.
O Rāma, be gracious, O remover of all afflictions, O most excellent one, O destroyer of the ocean of compassion! ||3||
O Lord of Śrī, O All-pervading One composed of splendor, forgive all my offenses and have mercy upon me!
O Giver of Fearlessness, you who have performed vast acts of merit for the sake of [removing] the cause of birth and so forth, you are my supreme refuge. 4.
He practiced the yoga of Yama and the other [limbs], yet he did not abandon the enjoyment of the objects prescribed for him.
O Lord of the Abode of the Universe, having spoken to me today, remove my threefold sufferings this very day.
Listen to this account, which is full of glory, by which even a wicked person may immediately attain whatever state he desires.
O Lord of Ascetics, although I am pierced by passion and other afflictions, grant me today that faultless [state] born from the company of the virtuous.
Indeed, by the mere glance of you, the great performer of benefit, one may attain liberation in a supreme instant.
O Lord of Sītā, let there be salutation to You; be gracious, O Rāma, who art the master of all; be gracious! ||7||
Born from the basin-like lap of Kausalyā, embraced by the creeper of Sītā,
watered by Daśaratha, and raised high by the great branches of his brothers;

May the wish-fulfilling tree that is Śrī Rāma bear for you the desired fruits of true merit—fruits that grant bliss to those who take refuge in its shade, which is expert at shattering the fierce heat of the Rākṣasa. ||8||
Thus ends the Śrī Rāmacandra Stotra composed by the venerable Paṇḍitācārya Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
